Therefore L=r, printed V=r-pi*r^3/6 and A=pi*r^2/2. The resulting w=1/10-pi/6000 is an admissible printed candidate with A=pi/200. Independently, I_gamma(v)<=sqrt(v) by Cauchyâ€“Schwarz and I0(v)>=sqrt(2v) for v<=1/2, so the product quantile map has Lipschitz constant<=1/sqrt(2). independent_verification.geometry_check: The upper density is pi(R-s)/2 with R=1/2+1/pi. The active graph R-sqrt(r^2-(1-t)^2) lies in this zone since r<2/pi. No minimality of this constructed set is assumed; the contradiction is to the unrestricted parametric infimum.
